$comment: HAND-MAINTAINED. Every deviation from what fal's own OpenAPI document says — and nothing else.
This file is deliberately its own file, and deliberately almost empty. The generator's whole claim is that
the types come from the provider's published schema; an overlay is that claim being broken for a stated,
dated, sourced reason. Folded into curation.json or pricing.json an exception would read like an ordinary
row. Here it cannot: an entry in this file is a thing a reviewer has to justify.
Overlay kinds, each requiring `reason` + `source` + `verified`:
enumAdd              a value the endpoint accepts that the schema omits
enumRemove           a value the schema lists that the endpoint rejects
rangeOverride        a HARD bound the schema states wrongly (a request outside it is refused)
rangeSoft            a bound that is advisory — warn, never refuse
typeOverride         the declared type is wrong on the wire
denyParam            a declared parameter that must never be sent
shapeClass           force a shape class the classifier cannot infer
durationsAreSeconds  a bare `duration` number whose unit the schema does not state
note                 documentation only; changes no type and no check
ANTI-ROT: an overlay naming a parameter the schema no longer declares FAILS codegen. An exception that has
outlived the thing it excepted is worse than no exception — it is a claim about a wire that no longer exists.
Wave 1d shipped ZERO overlays across all 140 curated endpoints. The v0.3.x roster widening added the
first two, and both are `note` kind: documentation only, changing no type and no check — the schema and
the generated types are still exactly what fal published. They record what fal's own PROSE gets wrong
about `fal-ai/lightx/relight` (see `endpoints` below).
Six things the roster widenings might have needed a real overlay for turned out to be general LOWERING
RULES rather than exceptions, and were implemented in scripts/codegen-fal.ts instead — which is the right
home for anything true of fal generally rather than of one endpoint:
• the OPEN ENUM idiom (`anyOf: [{enum: [...]}, {type: "string"}]`, "these values or any other
string"), which flux-pro/v1.1-ultra spells for `aspect_ratio`. An unlisted value there warns
rather than erroring, because refusing it would reject a request fal accepts;
• MEDIA detection. fal documents a `ui.field` hint and emits one exactly once across these
snapshots, so the parameter's own name is the primary source (`image_url`, `mask_url`,
`audio_url`) and `ui.field` is the override. That rule has an escape hatch by design — a name
fal spells in a way the heuristic cannot see would be stated here, by hand;
• the LANGUAGE NAME table. fal's speech endpoints spell a language four ways — a bare subtag at
Wizper, a subtag with a region at xAI, a capitalised name at MiniMax, and a name with a country
at Gemini — and the mapping back to BCP-47 primary subtags is a rule about fal rather than about
any one endpoint. A name the table does not know simply does not reach the row's `languages`,
which is a visible gap rather than an invisible guess;
• the CODEC name table, on the same argument. `wav`, `pcm` and `linear16` all mean signed 16-bit
little-endian PCM; `ogg` and `m4a` are containers that carry more than one codec and are
deliberately absent, because mapping `ogg` to Vorbis would be a guess about a file whose Opus arm
is on the same enum;
• the three-state `factors` rule at upscale (a range, a closed set, or none at all), which reads
`fal-ai/aura-sr`'s `const 4` and `fal-ai/recraft/upscale/crisp`'s missing field without either
being an exception to anything;
• the `aspect_ratio` value `"auto"`, which twenty rows offer and which no canonical `ratios` list
carries. `AspectRatio` is a SHAPE — a preset or a `W:H` spelling — and there is
no canonical word for "you decide", the same refusal `durationSeconds` makes for `"auto"` because it
is not a length. It costs almost nothing: `"auto"` is the schema DEFAULT on 17 of those 20 rows, so
omitting `aspectRatio` already sends it, and on the three where it is a distinct choice
`providerOptions.fal.aspect_ratio` reaches the wire as written. Every OTHER member of a closed
`aspect_ratio` enum must reach the row — including decimal spellings like `"2.35:1"` and `"19.5:9"` —
and codegen now FAILS on any it cannot place, naming the endpoint and the member. This bullet is the
rule's review: its absence from this list is why an integers-only pattern went unnoticed in 0.3.0.
The two exceptions the roster does contain are not overlays and do not belong here —
• `fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2`'s real `model` wire field is recorded per-id in data/fal/curation.json
(`allowsModelProperty`), because it is a routing fact about the endpoint, not a correction to its schema;
• the unpriced endpoints are recorded in data/fal/pricing.json as `unpriced` reasons.
Both are statements the schema agrees with. Only a disagreement lands here.

fal-ai/lightx/relight.reason: fal's own prose names a parameter that does not exist. Both `relight_parameters` and `relit_cond_img_url` describe themselves in terms of `relight_condition_type` ("required for relight_condition_type='ic'", "Required for relight_condition_type='ref'/'hdr'"), and no such field is declared anywhere in the document — the wire field is `relit_cond_type`, with the same four values (ic | ref | hdr | bg, default ic). Recorded rather than corrected: the TYPES are right, and a caller reading fal's page needs to know which of the two spellings goes on the wire.

A conditional requirement OpenAPI cannot state, so unmodel does not check it: `required` is `["video_url"]` alone, but fal's prose says `relight_parameters` is required when the condition type is 'ic' — the DEFAULT — and that `relit_cond_img_url` is required for 'ref', 'hdr' and 'bg'. A request with neither is accepted by this validator and refused by fal. The nested object's own required field (`relight_prompt`) is likewise unchecked: FalPropSpec carries `items` for arrays but no `props` for objects, so `t: "object"` is checked only for being a record — the same precedented degradation as fal-ai/flux-general's `fill_image`, `controlnet` and `ip_adapter`.
